reader.requirement: At --std 85 the compiler must refuse a REDEFINES whose subject is separated from data-name-2 by any entry at the same scope that defines new character positions (an ordinary data entry, a 77 or 01 at the roots), and must accept the subject after intervening redefinitions of the same area, condition-names (88), subordinates of a redefinition and level-66 entries, which define no new positions.
reader.edition-search: Grepped src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Compiler/Binding/Passes/ResolveRedefinesPass.cs, src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Compiler/Binding/Passes/ClassifyRedefinesClassesPass.cs, src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Compiler/Binding/DataBinder.cs#RedefinesDataName2/#ScreenDataNameShape and the grammar rule CobolData.g4 redefinesClause for CobolVersion, IsAtLeast, Std, Version., ConstructRegistry, DialectBehavior, ReservedWords and EditionContext edition properties: none. The only diagnostics sink is src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Compiler/Binding/EditionContext.cs#Error, which records the error with no edition test. REDEFINES is ungated in the grammar.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no: the same FirstInterveningStorage test runs at every --std; sr11_bad_sib draws the same COBOL2739 at --std 2023
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witness is the legal half only (redefinitions, an 88 and a redefinition's subordinates between, at 05 and 01); the refusal half (an ordinary sibling, a 77 or 01 root, a redefinition of a different item between) and a level-66 entry between are not exercised

reader.notes: The 1985 SR11 is the 2023 SR10 word for word apart from 'character positions' for 'storage areas'; the one screen implements it over the subject's sibling scope, or the subject's own section's roots at level 01/77. The diagnostic cites §2023:13.18.44.3 SR10 at --std 85, a citation of another edition, not a behaviour fault.
